title: Stanley Ellis (linguist) — Wikipedia
content: In June 1979, he correctly identified that a tape released by police that purported to be from the Yorkshire Ripper was by a hoaxer... Ellis had located the speaker to the Wearside area by comparing his speech with that of a recording made whilst studying the dialect of Washington.

citations.quote: Ellis had located the speaker to the Wearside area by comparing his speech with that of a recording made whilst studying the dialect of Washington.
citations.used_for: LIKELIHOOD RATIO 1 — best_match(wearside_survey_recordings_washington): P(questioned sample best-matches the Wearside/Washington SED comparison recording | speaker truly from Wearside/Sunderland) vs P(same | speaker from elsewhere). DIRECTION strongly positive and root-validated as a DIRECTIONAL fact: Stanley Ellis localized the speaker by comparing the tape against his own SED fieldwork, specifically a recording of the Washington dialect, and the Castletown/Southwick comparison speaker's 'segmental pronunciations, intonation patterns, rhythm and tempo closely resembled those of the questioned speaker', while similarities FELL OFF moving north — a positive co-localization gradient. GROUND TRUTH confirms direction: John Humble (DNA-identified 2005/2006) had 'spent his life on the Ford Estate in Sunderland, just across the River Wear from Castleton' — the exact region Ellis named. BUT no source publishes a numeric P(match|hypothesis) or a quantified false-match rate; the judgment was auditory/comparative, not a measured likelihood ratio. Hence direction_only for the NUMBER even though the direction traces to root primary observation.->wearside_sunderland_castletown
